title: Sonny and the Little Frog | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the little quokka hears a tiny frog singing a bedtime song beside a moonlit pond, and sits quietly to listen as the song grows slower and slower. A soft and soothing story from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales, made for tired little ears.
narration:
The evening had settled softly over the Australian bush, like a warm blanket tucking everything in. The sky was deep and still, and a round white moon hung low over the pond, turning the water to silver.

Sunny the little quokka was wandering along the edge of the bush, her paws quiet on the damp earth, when she heard something. A tiny sound. A small, sweet sound. A song.

She stopped and listened very carefully. There, sitting on a lily pad in the middle of the pond, was the tiniest green frog she had ever seen. And he was singing.

It was a slow, murmuring sort of song — not loud at all — soft as the sound of water breathing. Sunny crept a little closer and sat down on a mossy log at the water's edge.

"What are you singing?" she whispered.

The little frog blinked one golden eye at her. "A bedtime song," he said, "for the water lilies. They close up their petals at night, and they like to have a song to help them sleep."

Sunny looked at the lilies. One by one, their white petals were folding inward, slowly, gently, like tiny hands coming together.

The frog began to sing again. His song drifted across the still water. It was slower this time. And slower still.

Sunny's eyes felt very heavy. She rested her cheek on her soft paws and breathed the cool, green, pond-scented air. Somewhere in the reeds, the frog's song grew quieter. Quieter. And then both of them were asleep.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, little frog. Goodnight, little one.
